en: Khiva: A Museum Under the Open Sky

intro.uz: Bu — Xivaga borgan sayyohning blogidagi yozuv. Oʻqishdan oldin oʻylab koʻring: nega Xivani «ochiq osmon ostidagi muzey» deb atashadi?

paragraphs.en: Day 3 of my trip around Uzbekistan, and I think I have found my favourite place. After a long drive across the desert from Bukhara, we arrived in Khiva late in the afternoon. The sun was going down, and the old city walls were glowing orange. I had seen photos before, of course, but nothing had prepared me for how beautiful it looked in real life.

The old part of Khiva is called Itchan Kala, which means the inner town. It is surrounded by thick mud-brick walls, and you enter it through one of four gates. Inside, there are almost no modern buildings, just narrow streets, madrasas, mosques, minarets and palaces. In 1990, Itchan Kala became the first place in Uzbekistan to be added to the UNESCO World Heritage List. Walking around, I could easily see why people call Khiva a museum under the open sky.

The first thing I noticed was a short, wide tower covered in blue and green tiles. This is Kalta Minor, which means the short minaret. Our guide told us that the khan had planned it to be much taller, but he had died before it was finished, and the work was never completed. Even unfinished, it has become a symbol of the city.

The next morning, I visited the Juma Mosque. From the outside it looks quite simple, but inside there is a huge hall with more than two hundred carved wooden columns. Light comes in through openings in the roof, and the hall feels calm and cool, even on a hot day. I sat there for twenty minutes without saying a word.

In the evening, I climbed the Islam Khoja Minaret, the tallest in Khiva. The stairs were dark and steep, so I had to hold the wall all the way up. But the view from the top was worth it: the whole old town lay below me, with its domes and towers, and the flat land stretched to the horizon.

My advice? If you go to Khiva, stay at least two nights. Explore early in the morning or late in the afternoon, when it is cooler and there are fewer tourists. And wear comfortable shoes, because you will walk a lot!
